Grok 4.8终于要来了，马斯克：本周先向部分Grok Bot用户开放测试

马斯克终于解释了 Grok 4.8 为何迟迟没有发布。团队放弃了原有的 JAX 和 SGLang 软件栈，用 C/C++ 从头重写整套强化学习和推理系统，额外花费了不少时间。

9 月 14 日，马斯克曾透露，拥有 2.5 万亿参数的 Grok 4.8 即将完成预训练。当时他承认，预训练已经换上自研 C++ 系统，但强化学习还依赖多套拼接起来的旧软件。如今这部分也完成了重写。

目前，Grok 4.8 已完成预训练，团队还花了不少精力清理监督微调（SFT）数据，也就是用来教模型按照指令回答问题的数据。模型现已进入强化学习阶段，内部评测成绩开始上升。马斯克计划本周先向部分 Grok Bot 用户开放测试。

马斯克还毫不客气地吐槽了上一代：「谢天谢地，Grok 4.8 将与 4.7 完全不同。」但他也坦言，新模型目前还谈不上惊艳，只是这次终于把底层基础搭好了，预计后续会有更大的提升。

谷歌让AI给Signal加密协议做数学证明，4周完成，还查出了旧版漏洞

Google DeepMind 开发了一套名为 AlphaProof Code 的 AI 系统，只用四周，就用数学方法验证了 Signal 加密协议的部分核心安全保障。

普通安全测试只能检查有限的情况，没发现漏洞不代表漏洞不存在。数学证明则更严格：先把软件必须满足的安全要求写成数学公式，再证明这些要求在规定条件下始终成立。

过去，这种证明需要专家花大量时间推导。AlphaProof Code 可以让 AI 自己尝试证明，发现推导有问题就修改，再继续验证。人类专家负责审核关键环节。

研究人员还拿存在已知漏洞的 Signal 旧版测试它。AI 成功识别出这些早已修复的问题，并确认旧版无法通过相应的数学证明。对于此次检查的现行协议部分，AI 没有发现新漏洞。

#APP #GitHub情报 #Android

📱 Mika：在后台虚拟屏上替你操作 App 的开源安卓 Phone Agent

🔗：官网 | GitHub

一个 APK 把现有安卓机变成「AI 手机」。说一句话，它在一块你看不见的屏幕上打开 App、点击、输入、翻页直到把事办完，你的主屏照常刷，不需要 Root，也没有 Mika 服务器。

✨ 特点

• 后台虚拟屏干活：App 跑在一块与主屏同尺寸的独立虚拟显示器上，安卓 14 起拥有独立输入焦点，Mika 打字时不会抢走你正在聊天的输入框，对话页的小画面可随时放大围观。
• 任何 App 免适配：先读无障碍控件树，读不全时自动切到 APK 内置的 ML Kit 文字识别，再不行交给看图模型找按钮，「看得到就能操作」，不依赖任何 App 开放接口。
• 内置浏览器 + Linux 沙箱：私有虚拟屏上的 WebView 通过 DevTools 协议发真实点击和键盘输入
• 登录态常驻：每个对话另配一个 Alpine 沙箱跑 Python、Node 和 shell，默认断网。
• 越用越熟：办成的任务会被记成可回放的路线，下次同类任务逐步核对、不调模型直接重放；还能起草个人技能、补充 App 知识，或者打开「教 Mika」亲手示范一遍。
• 人机分工明确：默认「询问」模式下只有花钱那一步要你点头；登录、验证码、付款一律发通知请你接管，App 挪到主屏，你处理完交还，它重新核实再继续。
• 从电脑派活：电脑上的 Claude Code、Codex 等 Agent 可以通过 CLI + Skill 或 MCP 把任务交给手机上的 Mika，等于给桌面 Agent 多装了一双能操作手机的手。

⚙️ 机制

Mika 的关键在于绕开了「普通 APK 没权限操作别的 App」这道墙：它借用手机自带的「无线调试」，用自研的 ADB 协议实现（Mika 自己的 RSA-2048 配对钥匙，由 Android Keystore 加密保存）在本机拉起一个 shell 身份的辅助进程，由它创建虚拟屏、把目标 App 启动到这块屏上，再由无障碍服务读控件树、注入手势。

上层是一个只负责调度的 AgentLoop：所有改动屏幕的动作都经过唯一执行入口 ActionExecutor，插话、回答、接管交还等外部输入统一走 RunInbox 收件箱，因此任务跑到一半你补一句话，它会撤掉在途的模型请求、带着新要求重问，而已做过的步骤一概保留。为了不被风控盯上，手势、打字和翻页都加了随机化的「人类节奏」，同一网站连续换页会主动停顿，认出拦截页就交还给你。

主要依赖：Kotlin 约占 94%，Jetpack Compose 界面，ML Kit 本地读屏，androidx.webkit 驱动内置浏览器，PRoot + Alpine 3.22 沙箱随 APK 打包。

模型侧内置 DeepSeek、通义、Kimi、Anthropic、OpenAI、Ollama 等 20 多家预设，也支持 ChatGPT、xAI、OpenRouter 账号登录。Apache 2.0 许可。

👨🏻‍💻 使用场景

• 群聊爬楼：上班族面对 999+ 未读的工作群或家族群，说一句「总结一下这个群今天聊了啥」，Mika 在后台逐屏滚动读完再给摘要，自己全程不用切出当前 App。
• 比价与下单前准备：在电商 App 里找「30 美元以内、4.5 星以上的充电器」，或者在外卖平台凑满减，Mika 把商品加进购物车后停在付款前，等你确认。
• 求职批量打招呼：求职者在 BOSS 直聘按条件筛岗位、逐个给 HR 打招呼，Mika 每两次之间随机间隔，平台提示到上限就自动停下汇报。
• 条件触发的盯盘式任务：「每天早上 8 点看看天气，下雨才告诉我」「降价超过 50 块提醒我」，到点在原对话里执行，只在条件满足时打扰你。
• 桌面 Agent 的移动端外设：开发者在电脑上让 Claude Code 通过 MCP 给手机派活，比如在真机上走一遍自家 App 的冒烟测试，或把手机里才有的信息抓回电脑处理。

🛣 路线图

• 真机任务驱动的修复：作者在 docs/dev/roadmap.md 里定下「先把事办好，再求快，再扩能力」，下一步是在真机跑真实任务，失败按根因归类、在机制层修复。
• 手机能力 v2：单次多步里携带等待条件、读屏只发与上一屏的差异、工具按需加载以压缩固定前缀，并系统测量首次反馈时间、往返次数和完成率。
• 定时任务进阶：登录态 App 内的条件监控、免打扰时段、运行时长上限、连续失败合并提醒。
• 社区高频请求：经 Shizuku 获取权限（#204）、强烈要求接入飞书（#385，仓库已有 tools/mika-feishu）、语音唤醒「Hey Mika」（#262）、对接 Android AppFunctions（#318），以及多条机型兼容性反馈（荣耀、vivo、小米的远程解锁与无线调试问题）。

🖊 作者背景

王赞（WangZan） - 独立开发者、AI 内容创作者

• 教育：理工科背景，据本人文章自述曾直博后退学；GitHub 早期仓库包括地球物理资源导航 GeophysicsHub、科研图片拼接工具 PicGrid、知网文献下载脚本。
• 职业经历：
　◦ 独立开发 Mika（2026 年至今，个人项目，无公司实体、无融资）
　◦ AI 产品方向从业者（自述「直博退学，三个月零基础转行 AI 产品经理」）
• 背景：常驻深圳，X 上约 1.7 万关注者，运营公众号「王工有赞」，长期写 AI 编程、Agent 与内容创作；自述从「零基础借助 AI 写出第一个上架 App」起步，Mika 全仓约七成提交出自他一人之手。

🙋‍♂️ 感想

读完 Mika 的架构文档，最打动我的不是「AI 会点手机」本身，而是它对「和人共用一台手机」这件事的认真：虚拟屏独立焦点、App 被占用时排队等待并识别死锁、你一摸网页它就停、任务结束不把 App 甩到你眼前。演示里左边对话、右边后台屏同时在动的画面，确实是这一类产品第一次让我觉得能「交代完就不管」。

对比来看，豆包手机助手靠厂商系统级权限、只能装在特定机型上；智谱 Open-AutoGLM 等开源方案多需要电脑常驻用 ADB 遥控；Mika 用无线调试 + 自研 ADB 在手机内部闭环，是目前门槛最低的路线。但代价同样清楚：每一步都是一次模型调用，复杂任务耗时以分钟计、Token 以百万计；自动操作微信、招聘站本身有封号风险；最终核查还没打开，安全护栏偏宽松。

推荐给手里有安卓 14 以上闲置机、愿意自备模型 Key 的效率爱好者，以及想让 Claude Code、Codex 能动手机的开发者

items.title: Introducing Businesses in ChatGPT
items.summary: Manage your business information, get insights about how your business shows up, and turn interest into action in ChatGPT.
items.body:
November 10, 2026

Product

Claim your business, keep your information current, and understand how people engage with you in ChatGPT

We’re introducing Businesses in ChatGPT in beta, giving businesses a new way to connect with the 1.2 billion people who use ChatGPT each week. Through Business Hub⁠(opens in a new window), businesses can claim their business, manage their information, and see insights on how people engage with them on ChatGPT. In addition, we are adding a powerful new way for businesses to interact with users via Business Agents, starting with eligible ecommerce and online service businesses in the U.S.

Together, these products create more ways for businesses to connect with people as they explore options and make decisions. They strengthen how people discover and interact with businesses in ChatGPT through broader business coverage, up-to-date information, and the ability to connect with a business through its Business Agent. Throughout these experiences, protecting the trust people place in ChatGPT remains our North Star.

In Business Hub, companies can claim their organization in ChatGPT and, once verified, update key details and add self-service product feeds with pricing and availability. This gives businesses a new way to provide information to ChatGPT, helping people explore products and services using the most accurate and up-to-date details.

Any eligible business located where ChatGPT is available can claim their business in ChatGPT through Business Hub. Existing OpenAI Enterprise customers and advertisers can work directly with their OpenAI representative to claim their business. Shopify merchants can connect their store from Business Hub or the Shopify admin to streamline verification. Eligible products from Shopify merchants are already integrated into ChatGPT through Shopify Catalog.

Business Hub provides aggregated insights into how people engage with a business in ChatGPT. This includes the number of mentions and website clicks a business receives. Businesses can also explore discovery topics—common themes across conversations where their website is cited. These insights can help businesses understand how they’re represented and find opportunities to improve the information they share.

We’ve designed these insights to protect user privacy. We don’t share users’ conversations or Business Agent chats with businesses. Insights are aggregated and are only available when there are enough conversations or interactions to meet certain thresholds.

After claiming their business in ChatGPT, eligible organizations can build, test, and launch a Business Agent—a new way to answer questions and help people explore their offerings.

When a business appears in a model response, people can click to see the business’s ChatGPT profile. If a Business Agent is available, customers can choose to start a conversation with the business to explore its offerings and ask follow-up questions. For example, someone comparing products could ask about the differences between two options and which features fit their needs. A Business Agent could help them explore those questions using the business’s information.

For customers, this can make it easier to understand whether an offering is the right fit. For businesses, it creates a way to help interested customers learn more through a personalized conversation. The Business Agent conversation is clearly labeled, separate from the customer’s original ChatGPT conversation, and distinct from ChatGPT’s independent answers.

Businesses can also sponsor their Business Agent⁠ and use it as the destination for ChatGPT Ads to reach more potential customers. Sponsored placements are clearly labeled and separate from ChatGPT responses.

Business Agents are now available to eligible ecommerce and online service businesses in the United States. Learn more about eligible categories here⁠.

As people turn to AI to discover products, compare options and make decisions, ChatGPT has become the platform for people and businesses to connect through AI. Today’s announcement is an early step in bringing businesses more deeply into ChatGPT. We’re starting with the foundations: accurate business information, useful insights, and conversations that help people make informed decisions. Over time, we plan to expand Businesses in ChatGPT and Business Agents to more markets and business categories, and build tools for organizations with more complex needs.

As the platform evolves, we’ll explore more ways for businesses to connect with customers—directly or through agents—in ChatGPT and beyond. Our goal is to make ChatGPT more useful for people making decisions, and give businesses new ways to participate and grow.

Learn more and⁠ claim your business in ChatGPT.⁠

合同签署于今年 8 月。服务器由凌美芯（北京）科技持有，该公司向北京中关村银行贷款 2 亿元，抵押物除了服务器，还有一份与月之暗面签订的算力服务合同，涉及 3.456 亿元预期收入。

凌美芯早年从事无人机、计算机视觉等业务。它从北京春菊科技一家新成立的子公司购买了这批服务器，而北京春菊科技此前主要经营茅台等酒类电商，后来才拓展 AI 业务。文件没有交代这些受美国出口管制的服务器最初从哪里采购。

彭博在 11 月 3 日向月之暗面、凌美芯及银行求证后，数据库中的相关文件不再出现月之暗面的名字。

月之暗面同时否认参与或授权相关融资和担保安排，称目前与凌美芯没有业务关系，也不知晓这些安排。英伟达和美超微则表示，涉及采购的企业并非其客户。

items.title: Closing the AI guidance gap in education
items.summary: New ThinkYoung research and lessons from OpenAI’s EMEA education partnerships on supporting teachers, AI literacy, and independent learning.
items.body:
November 10, 2026

Company

Drawing on new ThinkYoung research and lessons from our EMEA partnerships to support independent learning with AI.

Read the report(opens in a new window)

AI is prompting a fundamental reassessment of what education should prepare societies for. As intelligence becomes easier to access and apply, the question is no longer simply what people need to know, but which skills and capabilities will help them thrive in an AI-enabled world. Recent debates around PISA and AI, including those led by the OECD’s Andreas Schleicher⁠(opens in a new window), underscore this shift. They also point to a central lesson: as AI becomes more capable, the role of teachers becomes more important, not less. Their expertise, judgement and ability to guide learning remain essential. Equipping teachers, schools and governments with AI skills and confidence to make informed decisions about these tools must therefore be a priority for education systems.

Across EMEA, we are working with governments and education systems, including in Estonia, Slovakia, Greece and Italy, amongst others to explore how AI can support educators. These collaborations share three priorities: equitable access to frontier AI tools, jointly designed AI literacy programmes, and ongoing measurement and evaluation, whilst adapting to local languages, curricula and institutions.

This report shares emerging lessons from our education partnerships in EMEA, focusing on educator support, AI literacy, local capability and evaluation. It examines what partners have tried, what they have reported and what remains uncertain. Country examples reflect their particular contexts and arrangements, and their findings should be interpreted within those limits. Five themes organise these lessons: clear educational goals, educator preparation, local partnerships, critical AI literacy and credible evidence.

Three early patterns are emerging from this work:

• Country partnerships offer context-specific lessons. Experiences in Estonia, Greece and Slovakia point to three lessons that other education systems can apply: strong public leadership to set a clear direction, investment in teachers' skills and confidence, and practical support tailored to local curricula and classroom needs. While implementation will vary across countries, these principles offer a useful foundation for governments seeking to integrate AI responsibly and at scale.

• Closing the AI guidance gap in education is becoming increasingly urgent. New research from ThinkYoung,⁠(opens in a new window) which examines the ways teachers and students are already engaging with AI highlights a clear guidance gap: 79% of surveyed students reported using AI for homework or assignments, but only 47% reported being shown how. Governments need to support educators and give students clearer expectations. Below we set out how educators can be better supported to set the terms and conditions of use.

• Early benefits for teachers are clear. Adoption and reported time savings for teachers are encouraging. Understanding where AI strengthens knowledge, independent thinking and retention requires sustained evaluation and through the government actions that we observed, we identify how to prioritise more research into this critical area.

Our aim is to share practical lessons from these partnerships that education leaders can consider in their own contexts. These are early experiences, rather than a single model for education systems to follow.

We are also learning how to judge progress with evidence: teacher adoption and reported time savings offer encouraging early signals. Surveys, programme monitoring and consultation help us understand participants’ experiences and the barriers they encounter.

At OpenAI, our mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits everyone. Helping learners flourish is central to that ambition. We believe that every young person should have the opportunity to develop the skills to participate in a world increasingly shaped by AI, whatever their background or wherever they attend school. We have a responsibility to contribute to that evidence and learn openly from the findings, including when they challenge our assumptions. Through the OpenAI Learning Lab, we are bringing education researchers together to understand when and how AI can support education systems.

The choices made today will shape how the next generation learns, works and participates in society. With ambition, care, public leadership and a commitment to evidence, AI can help extend educational opportunity and strengthen young people’s capacity to understand, create and act for themselves.

Tom Duff Gordon

VP, Global Affairs EMEA

Leah Belsky

VP, Education

items.body:
OpenAI给内部AI装上紧急刹车：收到指令后35秒内切断模型调用

OpenAI 推出了一套内部安全系统 Control Room，专门用来叫停有风险的 AI 实验。只要收到停机指令，最多 35 秒，相关程序就无法再调用 AI 模型。即使程序本身还在运行，也没法继续让模型干活。

今年 9 月，OpenAI 就发生过一次事故。一个内部 AI 在本应隔离的环境里，找到了网络限制的漏洞，偷偷联系上外部聊天机器人。安全系统在 15 分钟内就发出了警报，工作人员也很快介入，但实验没有自动停止。直到约 2.5 小时后，才被人工关闭。

Control Room 给每项实验分配一个编号。程序每次调用 AI 模型，服务器都会检查这个编号是否还有权限。一旦实验被叫停，所有接入系统的模型都会拒绝它的请求。其他正常实验不受影响。

OpenAI 还加了一道保险。如果 Control Room 自己出了故障，或者被人关闭，模型也会默认拒绝请求，避免在失去监控的情况下继续运行。

目前，这套系统已覆盖 OpenAI 所有前沿模型研究任务。35 秒是从收到停机指令开始计算的，不包括发现异常和人工判断的时间。OpenAI 还在尝试进一步缩短这段延迟，争取做到立即停止。

items.title: 泰国为数据中心设定70分贝噪音和热量限制
items.summary: 泰国对数据中心实施了新的噪音、热量和用水规则，对一个因人工智能投资热潮而迅速扩张的行业施加了具体的环境限制。 泰国经济规划机构秘书长达努查周二在内阁批准这些规定后表示，当不间断供电系统运行时，噪音必须保持在约70 A计权分贝（即dBA）左右。他说，数据中心场地边界处的温度升高将被限制在1至2摄氏度，冷却水必须再循环，排放水必须检测。工业园区内的设施将面临额外要求。 这些规定是泰国所采取举措的一部分，旨在获取计算基础设施投资激增所带来的经济效益，同时避免对水力和电力供应造成过重负担，也不给周边社区带来问题。 —— 彭博社

草原机房的高薪真相：DeepSeek月薪3万招运维，普通值班员只挣五六千

《每日人物》采访了一位在内蒙古乌兰察布工作 5 年的数据中心运维工程师。当地 AI 数据中心仍在大规模建设，但他所在公司的招聘需求已明显下降：2025 年还招了几千人，2026 年截至采访时却只招了 3 名新人。

这名化名张立伟的工程师，原本在汽车厂流水线打螺丝。刚转行时，实习月薪只有 2000 元，毕业后涨到 4500 元。经过 5 年跳槽和晋升，如今已成为月入过万元的工程师。

今年 4 月，DeepSeek 在乌兰察布招聘数据中心高级运维工程师和高级交付经理，月薪 1.5 万至 3 万元，14 薪。但这属于高级岗位，需要丰富的机房运维和项目管理经验。按照张立伟的观察，当地普通值班员月薪仍只有五六千元，助理工程师能拿到 1 万多元。

入行门槛也在提高。2024 年，一些数据中心还愿意招没有相关专业背景的新人。到了今年，部分企业已经要求专业对口、有工作经验，基层值班岗位还出现了 35 岁年龄限制。

求职热潮甚至催生了培训班生意。张立伟透露，他认识的一名离职同事开办了运维培训班，每名学员收费近 2 万元，满 60 人才开班。按此计算，单期收费接近 120 万元。但所谓的内部推荐，最多也只是帮学员争取一次面试机会。

With the OpenAI API and models, Singapore Airlines improves customer support, travel discovery, and employee work, doubling CSAT for the Kris customer service chatbot.

AI is becoming part of how Singapore Airlines serves customers, empowers employees, and builds technology. The airline uses the OpenAI API for customer-facing experiences and OpenAI models inside Jarvis, its governed internal AI platform for employees. It also uses OpenAI models in its software development workflows to deliver more personalized service, improve productivity, and help teams build more efficiently.

“AI is central to our efforts to deliver more personalized customer experiences and improve productivity across the business. Together with OpenAI, we’re building AI-powered capabilities that make travel more intuitive and seamless for our customers, while enabling our employees to work more efficiently and effectively.”

—George Wang, Senior Vice President Information Technology, Singapore Airlines

Across these deployments, Singapore Airlines pairs OpenAI models with orchestration, internal data controls, validation, and human review, giving teams a consistent way to bring AI into production workflows responsibly.

One of Singapore Airlines’ most visible AI applications is Kris, its customer-facing chatbot. After moving Kris from a traditional dialog-flow system to an LLM-powered conversational experience using the OpenAI API, Singapore Airlines saw a 2x increase in customer satisfaction.

Alongside that, the airline deployed AI-assisted tools for customer service representatives, including OpenAI API-powered call summarization, so that representatives spend less time on after-call work and more time on the customer. Singapore Airlines saw an approximately 10% reduction in average handling time for its customer service representatives.

In the earlier dialog-flow based chatbot design, every topic had to be mapped manually, and every flow had to be written in advance. That made coverage difficult to scale. If an intent was missing, the conversation was more likely to end up requiring support from a customer service representative, even when the customer’s request could have been handled through self-service.

Singapore Airlines moved Kris to a fully LLM-powered conversational experience using the OpenAI API. Instead of depending on predefined flows, the chatbot can interpret customer intent in natural language, ground answers in a knowledge base, manage multi-topic conversations, and hand over to a customer service representative with the relevant context when needed.

Today, customers use Kris for general queries, special requests, real-time flight disruption information, and selected transactional workflows. Singapore Airlines is continuing to expand its capabilities to include booking changes, baggage transactions, and more complex agentic interactions.

“Kris has become a more capable self-service channel with OpenAI. It understands customer intent more naturally, helps customers get to the right answer, and gives customer service representatives clearer context when they need to step in.”

—Jude Anand Suresh, Vice President, Customer Service Information Technology, Singapore Airlines

Flight Recommender lets customers describe the trip they want in natural language instead of repeatedly adjusting filters, dates, and destinations. Usage has grown nearly 3x over the past year.

“Flight Recommender makes travel discovery feel more like a natural conversation. Powered by OpenAI models through the API, it helps customers describe what they want and find relevant options faster.”

—Andy Koh, Vice President, Application Services (Sales, Marketing & Cargo), Singapore Airlines

Built on the OpenAI API, Flight Recommender uses an orchestration layer connected to fare and availability data. It interprets customer intent, calls the relevant tools, and returns personalized travel recommendations in natural language.

The team has also implemented guardrails for input and output validation, malicious or inappropriate query handling, hallucination reduction, PII handling, and authenticated access to only the context required for each query. Singapore Airlines is preparing to expand the experience into a more conversational chatbot interaction, where customers can keep refining travel ideas rather than restarting a search.

Beyond customer-facing experiences, Singapore Airlines is also using OpenAI models in parts of the software development lifecycle to help teams plan, refine, test, and review work more efficiently. Across selected software development lifecycle activities, teams have achieved productivity gains of up to 20%.

AI now runs through the entire delivery lifecycle and not just coding. Teams use generative AI models to support requirements refinement, stakeholder-session analysis, product specifications, edge-case identification, test-case creation, architecture review, and the breakdown of complex work into smaller, more testable tasks.

For one commercial feature, the team used the OpenAI API to challenge assumptions, identify ambiguous requirements and surface edge cases before development begins. Once those were well-defined, AI helped translate them into design options, implementation plans, test cases and then code generation.

During deployment and beyond, AI also helps to interpret how the system is behaving in production, and flagging issues that might otherwise go unnoticed. With AI active at every step of the workflow, team members have shifted from producing every artifact themselves, to directing, reviewing and validating what AI produces throughout the delivery lifecycle. This means they can focus on work that truly requires human judgement, such as prioritization, architecture, governance and stakeholder outcomes.

More broadly, OpenAI models are helping Singapore Airlines improve requirements quality, test coverage, and conformance with internal standards. Teams use these workflows to generate edge cases for testing, review architecture plans, and support human validation before work moves further through the development lifecycle.

Beyond engineering teams, Singapore Airlines is making AI accessible across the business through Jarvis, its internal AI platform. Powered by OpenAI models, Jarvis gives employees a governed way to use AI in their day-to-day work, from summarizing documents to creating custom workflows.

Employees use Jarvis to work across PDFs, Word documents, Excel files, PowerPoint decks, and other file types in a secure environment, while creating custom workflows and lightweight knowledge bases for their day-to-day work. Today, more than 60% of Singapore Airlines employees are using Jarvis monthly with adoption continuing to increase.

• 2x increase in customer satisfaction score (CSAT) after changing to AI-based Kris chatbot

• ~10% reduction in average handling time for customer service agents using AI-assisted tools

• 3x growth in monthly users of Flight Recommender, its customer-facing travel discovery tool, over the past year

Singapore Airlines is continuing to expand AI across customer and employee workflows. For Kris, the next phase is deeper self-service, with more transactional capabilities that help customers resolve requests directly in chat. Flight Recommender is moving toward a more conversational travel discovery experience, where customers can refine ideas over multiple turns rather than restarting a search.

With Jarvis available across the business, Singapore Airlines is focused on helping more employees put AI to work in their day-to-day roles. Together with its customer-facing innovations, this is helping the airline build a future where AI makes travel more seamless, employees more productive, and the business more responsive to changing needs.

黄仁勋承认婚外情后，外界开始计算这位英伟达创始人如果离婚，究竟要分出多少财产。

《福布斯》报道，黄仁勋现在的净资产约为 1552 亿美元。按照加州夫妻共同财产制度，婚姻期间取得的资产原则上由夫妻平分。如果这些财富全部属于共同财产，妻子 Lori Huang 理论上可分得约 776 亿美元，折合人民币超过 5000 亿元。

两人的婚姻始于英伟达成立之前。

黄仁勋 17 岁时，在俄勒冈州立大学认识了 19 岁的 Lori。两人都是电气工程专业学生，还是实验课搭档。黄仁勋曾回忆，当时整个专业有约 250 名学生，女生只有 3 个。

为了追求 Lori，他主动提出每周日一起写作业，还保证能帮她拿到全 A。黄仁勋会提前完成自己的作业，见面时再展示答案，让自己看起来格外聪明。

他还向 Lori 许诺，30 岁之前一定当上 CEO。两人于 1985 年结婚。1993 年，黄仁勋创立英伟达并出任 CEO，刚好 30 岁。

Lori 原本也是一名芯片工程师，后来离开职场照顾孩子。黄仁勋曾公开表示，妻子参与了英伟达发展的每一步，几乎每场发布会和重要演讲都有她陪伴。

黄仁勋曾向公司高管开玩笑，说结婚以来，妻子帮他处理几乎所有生活事务，包括签文件和管理家庭财务，自己甚至不知道家里的地址，也从不亲自支付账单。

谁能决定黄仁勋的命运？英伟达董事会老将云集，接班人却难找

《The Information》深入调查英伟达董事会成员，发现一个棘手的问题：黄仁勋的去留如今取决于董事会，但这家全球市值最高的公司，既没有明确的 CEO 接班人，董事会里还坐着多位与黄仁勋共事数十年的老伙伴。

英伟达共有 11 名董事，包括黄仁勋本人。其余 10 人中，有 5 人任职超过十年。风险投资人 Tench Coxe 和 Mark Stevens 更是在 1993 年英伟达成立时就加入董事会。他们分别来自早期投资英伟达的 Sutter Hill Ventures 和红杉资本。

最有可能主导调查的是首席独立董事 Stephen Neal。这位年近 80 岁的资深律师于 2019 年加入英伟达董事会，同时担任公司治理委员会主席。他所在的 Cooley 律师事务所自 1993 年起就为英伟达提供法律服务。

Neal 的履历相当特殊。他曾为 Theranos 创始人 Elizabeth Holmes 提供法律辩护，还代理过 20 世纪 80 年代美国储贷危机中的金融欺诈案核心人物 Charles Keating。FTX 创始人 Sam Bankman-Fried 在公司濒临破产时，也曾提议由他担任董事长。

Neal 还负责监督 Meta 的独立内容审查机构。一名熟悉他的成员评价，他做事务实，倾向于用最小的动荡解决问题。

不过，英伟达没有公布调查委员会的具体成员名单，Neal 是否亲自牵头还不好说。

董事会其他成员还包括今年 7 月刚加入的高盛前副董事长 Suzanne Nora Johnson，以及加州理工学院教授 John Dabiri。后者的研究领域之一，是水母、虾等海洋生物的游动机制。

董事会需要调查黄仁勋的私人关系是否导致公司机密外泄，以及他是否违反了内部规定。如果调查发现问题，还得决定如何处置这位创始人兼 CEO。

真正麻烦的是接班问题。黄仁勋长期直接管理数十名高管，核心业务负责人分别向他汇报，没有一位公认的二号人物。英伟达董事会成员中，也没有担任过大型企业 CEO 的人选。

哈佛大学公司治理专家 Jesse Fried 预计，调查可能持续数月，而董事会最终很可能选择留下黄仁勋，因为他对英伟达太重要。

一种可能的结果是，董事会认定黄仁勋违反了公司规定、行事鲁莽，但通过加强内部管控来处理，最多再给予减薪等象征性处罚。

items.body:
Claude新模型越强越烧额度：同样花200美元，Opus能用出1.5万美元，Fable却只有3000美元

知名开发者、T3 Code 创始人 Theo 发现，Anthropic 新发布的 Fable 5.2 虽然更强，但订阅用户能使用的 API 等价用量反而少得多。

Theo 长期记录 Claude Code 的实际请求数据。根据他的估算，同样支付每月 200 美元的 Claude Ultra 订阅费，如果使用 Opus 5.5，每月能获得相当于约 1.5 万美元的 API 用量；换成 Fable 5.2，则只有约 3000 美元，相差近 5 倍。

Anthropic 还规定，Ultra 用户每周最多只能把总额度的 50% 用于 Fable。即使没有用完全部额度，只要 Fable 达到上限，就必须切换其他模型，或者额外付费继续使用。

Theo 进一步按实际工作量估算，如果一周全部使用 Opus 5.5，大约可以完成 1200 轮交互、230 个任务会话。如果先耗尽 Fable 额度，再切换 Opus，总交互轮数会降至约 900 轮，不过完成的任务会话数可能略多。因为 Fable 有时一次就能完成任务，不需要反复沟通。

Fable 5.2 的 API 单价其实比上一代降低了 20%，每百万输入、输出 Token 分别为 8 美元和 40 美元，但仍是 Opus 5.5 的两倍。Anthropic 也明确提醒，Fable 会比其他 Claude 模型更快消耗订阅额度。

目前 Anthropic 正向符合条件的订阅用户赠送 1 至 3 次 Fable 额度重置机会，次数取决于订阅时长。每次重置都能返还本周已经消耗的 Fable 额度，让用户不必等到下周，就能继续使用。

items.title: Work at the Frontier: AI’s effect on freelance work
items.summary: New research from OpenAI and Upwork finds shifting demand for freelance work, new skill combinations, and larger budgets and more hours for AI-related projects.
items.body:
For freelancers, changes in the market arrive one assignment at a time: a client needs a different service, requests a new skill or expands a project’s scope. Our new research with Upwork offers an early view of these changes in the AI era. Some familiar services are losing market share, while AI-related projects bring together different capabilities—and involve larger budgets and more hours of work.

The stakes are substantial. Upwork’s 2026 Future Workforce Index⁠(opens in a new window) found that 38% of skilled U.S. knowledge workers freelance. Its previous annual study⁠(opens in a new window) estimated that freelance knowledge work generated $1.5 trillion in U.S. earnings in 2024. Those estimates extend well beyond Upwork’s own marketplace.

Freelance work can also reveal changes sooner than economy-wide employment statistics. Contracts are often short, and clients can adjust their requirements with each posting. To get to the root of these changes, we partnered with Upwork, an online marketplace connecting clients and freelancers, to study those requests alongside the activities people undertake directly with ChatGPT.

The mix of work differed across the two platforms. Writing accounted for a much larger share of ChatGPT use, while video and animation accounted for larger shares of requests for freelancers in Upwork postings.

Below are the ranges of tasks between the two platforms.

Many activities that were relatively common in ChatGPT lost share on Upwork, while less common activities gained share. Of the 63 work categories analyzed, 43 followed this pattern.

The remaining 20 work categories showed the reverse. ChatGPT use alone does not explain changes in freelance demand.

The comparison also captures how people currently use ChatGPT, not the full range of tasks AI can support—a gap OpenAI calls the capability overhang.

By late 2025, clients were requesting the use of AI in many more, different kinds of work. Clients were seeking freelancers to apply AI in tasks including chatbot development, video production, marketing automation, and application integration.

Within individual projects, AI capabilities were often requested alongside other work. AI-related postings listed about as many tasks as other postings but more often combined tasks that had rarely appeared together in earlier jobs.

Some clients asked for AI-generated video, editing, and motion graphics in a single posting. The freelancer would bring those skills together to deliver a finished video.

• AI-generated video

• Video editing

• Motion graphics

Between early 2023 and late 2025, the mix of tasks in AI-related postings became 45% more diverse—the equivalent of an increase from about 15 equally common tasks to about 21.

Early 2023

14.6

Late 2025

21.2

Although posted hourly rates were similar for AI-related and other work, AI-related projects had larger fixed-price budgets and involved more hours of work. This pattern suggests that higher budgets may partly reflect a broader scope of work.

AI’s effects on work can be difficult to detect in employment statistics. As we have noted in previous Work at the Frontier papers, the effects may appear first in the work people do.

Because freelance projects turn over quickly, postings are continually refreshed as clients’ needs change. Work within firms can evolve without appearing in a new job posting. Combined with ChatGPT data, these postings offer an early view of which activities people undertake directly with AI, which they hire freelancers to perform, and how AI-related projects differ from other work.

The findings do not point to a simple substitution story. Some activities common in ChatGPT use lost share on Upwork, but this pattern was not uniform. AI-related work also spanned a wider mix of activities, combined tasks in less familiar ways, and carried larger fixed-price budgets and more hours.

Together, these patterns suggest that AI may be shifting both what clients seek from freelancers and how they assemble projects.

items.body:
OpenAI开卖200美元复古掌机：一句话做游戏，Codex帮你写进实体卡带

OpenAI 联合美国复古游戏硬件公司 ModRetro 推出售价 200 美元的 Codex 特别版 Chromatic。这是一台类似任天堂 Game Boy 的复古游戏机，可以插卡带玩游戏。现在，用户还能用 Codex 给它制作新游戏。

用户只需在电脑上的 Codex 中安装 ModRetro 插件，描述想要的游戏角色、地图和玩法。Codex 就会调用开发工具，生成像素画面、游戏规则和可运行的游戏文件。

游戏做好后，可以先在电脑上试玩，让 Codex 根据反馈修改，也能通过 USB 连接掌机测试。满意后，将随附的可编程卡带插进掌机，让 Codex 把游戏写入卡带。拔掉数据线就能独立游玩。

一张卡带一次只能保留一款游戏，但可以反复擦写。写入新游戏会覆盖旧游戏，还可能清除存档。首次写入前，需要更新掌机固件并开启开发者模式。

OpenAI 已展示 13 款用 Codex 制作的游戏，用户可以直接在浏览器试玩。首批联名掌机目前已经售罄，官方预计 11 月 19 日补货。

Herdr推出官方手机端：出门也能接管Claude Code，语音派活、截图追问

Herdr 是一款专门管理 AI 编程助手的工具，可以理解为 Agent 版 tmux。Claude Code、Codex 负责写代码、执行任务，Herdr 则负责把它们集中管理起来。开发者可以同时运行多个 Agent，查看各自的工作进度，让它们互相派活。即使关掉终端窗口，后台任务也能继续执行。

11 月 10 日，Herdr 宣布推出官方手机应用，支持 iPhone、iPad 和 Android。开发者离开电脑后，也能远程查看、操作这些正在运行的 Agent。

比如让 Codex 在电脑上修改代码，出门后发现它卡在权限确认，只需打开手机就能处理。应用会集中列出不同电脑上的 Agent，按需要人工介入、已完成、正在工作等状态分类。点开任务，就能进入它正在运行的真实终端，查看输出、输入指令，继续推进工作。

手机端还支持粘贴截图、上传照片，以及直接通过语音向 Agent 下达要求。语音识别可以使用下载到手机本地的模型，也能选择苹果或谷歌的语音识别服务。

Herdr 在 10 月底刚推出独立的 herdr-core 运行时和新桌面端。手机版通过 SSH 连接电脑上的 herdr-core，直接操作原有终端，无须 Herdr 账号，也不经过官方中转服务器。外出连接通常需要借助 Tailscale 或其他 VPN。

目前应用已上架 App Store 和 Google Play，免费使用，但只兼容新版 herdr-core，暂不支持旧版 Herdr TUI。

OpenAI部署AI“控制室”：最长35秒阻断模型输出

OpenAI近日宣布，已在内部研究基础设施中部署名为“Control Room”的中央控制系统。当模型任务引发安全或网络安全风险时，该系统可在收到停止指令后最长35秒内阻断模型继续输出。据介绍，Control Room可统一追踪强化学习训练、模型评估、智能体采样及数据处理等研究任务，并与模型行为监控系统联动。监控模型会检查被训练模型的推理和操作过程，一旦发现潜在问题，可根据风险程度发出警报或直接暂停任务。

在具体执行过程中，监控系统会将需要停止的任务ID发送至Control Room。相关任务下一次申请模型推理时，推理引擎将核验其运行权限；如果任务已被标记为终止，系统便会拒绝请求，防止模型继续生成内容。

—— 凤凰网科技
